title: Nonvanishing locus under restriction along an open immersion
statement: Let f : X → Y be an open immersion of schemes, let M be an O_Y-module, and let s be a global section of M. Under the canonical restriction isomorphism, the nonvanishing locus of the restricted section is the inverse image f⁻¹(Y_s), where nonvanishing means that the germ lies outside the maximal ideal times the stalk module.

source.place: Lemma 01CY, and properties.tex Lemma 01PV proof, affine translation

proof.text: The inverse structure-sheaf stalk isomorphism sends the germ of r on U to the germ of (f.appIso U).inv r on f(U). Prove this using germ_stalkMap and appIso_inv_app, cancelling the stalk isomorphism.

Represent a scalar stalk element by a germ and represent a module stalk element on a smaller common neighbourhood. The germ_smul identity and germ_restrictStalkNatIso_hom_app show that the additive restriction stalk isomorphism is compatible with the inverse ring stalk isomorphism.

A ring equivalence preserves units, hence preserves membership in the maximal ideal. By Submodule.smul_induction_on in both directions and the compatible additive stalk equivalence, membership in maximal ideal times the whole module is preserved. Apply this to the restricted section germ and use germ_res_apply to identify it with the original section germ. Negate the membership equivalence pointwise.

lean.statement: theorem nonvanishingLocus_restrict {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion f] (M : Y.Modules) (s : M.val.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)) : nonvanishingLocus (M.restrict f) ((M.restrictAppIso f ⊤).inv (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op s)) = f ⁻¹' nonvanishingLocus M s
